sources.citation: Taguchi, Yoshihisa 田口善久. 2010. 恭城県三江郷ミエン語(チャウコンメン)調査報告 [A brief sketch of Cao Kong Meng]. 千葉大学ユーラシア言語文化論集 12: 71-82.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress; §2.4 声調 (pp. 76-77) gives 7 tone categories and a phonetic tone alternation (tone 3 -> [33] before other tones). Describes Cao Kong Meng = 交公勉 of Shikou village, which Chinese sources group with Biao Min 标敏 (i.e. bje, not bmt). Read for identity: p. 72 fn. 7 says Taguchi 2005 treats the phonology of the neighbouring 'Mohimu' [mo55 çi31 muə31] variety (Litian/Xiaolitian/Niuweizhai villages) and calls it phylogenetically close to Iu Mien.

sources.citation: Taguchi, Yoshihisa 田口善久. 1999. 三江小栗田勉語語彙集 [A study of the vocabulary of Xiaolitian Yao language]. 言語文化論叢 (Papers on Languages and Cultures, Chiba University) 5: 1-28.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: §1 音韻体系 (pp. 2-3) covers consonants, glides, vowels, finals and tones only; no mention of stress/accent. Only prosodic remark (§1.5, p. 3): the original 8 Mienic tones have merged to 5, and in nouns the tone value of a syllable read in isolation or word-initially differs clearly from its value in non-initial syllables (e.g. tone 1 433/33, tone 2 55/31). Variety: Mien of Xiaolitian, Daliitian, Niuwei villages, Sanjiang township, Gongcheng county (= Taguchi 2005's 'Sanjiang Shimen Mian', which Glottolog files under bmt; identity with Biao Mon proper doubtful).

sources.citation: Luang-Thongkum, Theraphan. 1993. A view on Proto-Mjuenic (Yao). Mon-Khmer Studies 22: 163-230.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Image-only PDF; pp. 163-166 (abstract, background, list of field sites) read as page images: comparative reconstruction from the author's own field data; nothing on stress in the pages read. Its 'Muen' = Ao Yao / Bjao Muen of Jinxiu county (Luoxiang, Liucang), i.e. Ao Biao, not Biao Mon proper (Wikipedia's equation of Muen with Biao Mon is not what the paper says).
